intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass
experiences.description: Ski the world-famous slopes of Zermatt with stunning views of the Matterhorn. With over 360km of marked runs, this resort caters to all skill levels. Book slopes near the village base to maximize time after a late Day 1 arrival, starting fresh on Day 2. Stay in Zermatt village to walk to lifts each morning.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Explore the breathtaking Jungfrau region on guided snowshoe trails through pristine alpine landscapes. Trails depart directly from Grindelwald village center, making it ideal for those staying locally. A perfect mid-week activity after ski days, requiring no special equipment rental beyond snowshoes included in the tour.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz and optionally ride the historic Olympia Bob Run, one of the world's oldest natural ice bobsled tracks. Both attractions are within walking distance of St. Moritz village center, eliminating transfer time. Best enjoyed mid-afternoon when ice conditions are optimal.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening
experiences.description: Join a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner experience in a historic mountain chalet in Verbier village. Learn about centuries-old Alpine cheese-making culture while warming up after a day on the slopes. Restaurants are clustered in the village center, perfect for guests staying in Verbier accommodations.

experiences.name: Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure
experiences.description: Ride the iconic cable car to Glacier 3000 above Les Diablerets for panoramic views across four countries. Experience the Snow Bus ride across the glacier plateau and visit the Peak Walk suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks. The base station is a short walk from Les Diablerets village, ideal for a full afternoon excursion on a rest day from skiing.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport, take a budget train or bus toward Poschiavo via the Bernina Express route. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle in, unpack, and get a good night's rest after the long journey.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport or train station — look for a Migros or Coop grab-and-go sandwich or wrap (CHF 5–8) to keep costs low during transit.

day_by_day.notes: From Zurich HB, take the train to Chur, then connect to the Rhaetian Railway toward Tirano — alight at Poschiavo station. Journey takes approximately 4–5 hours. Book tickets in advance on SBB.ch for best prices. The B&B is a short walk or taxi ride from Poschiavo station. Keep luggage light for easy train travel.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty B&B breakfast, take a leisurely morning walk through the charming historic village of Poschiavo. Explore the Piazza Comunale, admire the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo) with its colorful Italianate architecture, and visit the Reformed Church of San Vittore. This is a free self-guided walking tour that gives you a feel for the unique Swiss-Italian culture of the Valposchiavo valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), a scenic alpine lake just a short walk from the village center. Walk along the lakeside path enjoying stunning winter mountain views. If the lake is partially frozen, it makes for incredible photography. Explore the surrounding snowy meadows and take in the crisp mountain air — a perfect free afternoon activity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village center for a relaxed evening. Browse the small local shops and pick up some budget-friendly Swiss chocolate or local Valposchiavo products as souvenirs. Enjoy a warm drink at a local café before heading back to the B&B.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pick up supplies at the local Coop or Migros supermarket in Poschiavo for a self-made picnic lunch by the lake — bread, cheese, salami, and fruit for around CHF 8–12.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — a local budget-friendly restaurant offering traditional Graubünden dishes like pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) or polenta with cheese. Expect CHF 18–25 for a main course.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to recover from jet lag and travel fatigue. Poschiavo sits at 1,014m elevation — take it easy to acclimatize before more strenuous activities. Wear warm layers as February temperatures can drop to -5°C to -10°C at night.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic Bernina Express train from Poschiavo up toward the Bernina Pass (2,253m) — one of the highest railway crossings in the Alps and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Ride up to Ospizio Bernina station and step out into a breathtaking high-alpine winter wonderland. The journey itself is spectacular with viaducts, glaciers, and snow-covered peaks. A short segment ticket costs approximately CHF 10–15.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Ospizio Bernina, enjoy free snowshoeing or winter hiking on the marked trails around Lago Bianco (White Lake), which is typically frozen solid in February. The frozen lake surrounded by glaciers and peaks is one of the most dramatic winter landscapes in Switzerland. Bring your own snacks and hot drinks in a thermos to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo in the late afternoon. Warm up at the B&B with a hot shower, then head out for a budget dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of hot soup and sandwiches from the B&B or supermarket to enjoy at Ospizio Bernina — saves significant money versus buying at mountain restaurants.
meals.dinner: Pizzeria/Trattoria in Poschiavo village — pizza or pasta dishes typically CHF 14–20. Look for the daily special (piatto del giorno) for best value.

day_by_day.notes: Dress in full winter gear for the Bernina Pass — temperatures at 2,253m can be -15°C to -20°C with wind chill in February. Wear waterproof boots, thermal layers, hat, gloves, and goggles. The train ride is approximately 30 minutes from Poschiavo. Check SBB.ch for timetables. Snowshoes can sometimes be rented in Poschiavo village for CHF 15–20/day.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Diavolezza ski area, accessible from Diavolezza station on the Bernina railway line (one stop above Ospizio Bernina). Diavolezza is one of the most spectacular ski resorts in the Alps, offering stunning views of the Morteratsch Glacier and Piz Palü. Purchase a half-day ski pass (approximately CHF 45–55) for the morning session. Rent ski equipment at the resort base (CHF 35–45 for skis, boots, and poles).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza in the early afternoon to maximize your lift pass value. The resort offers runs for all levels — beginners can stick to the easier blue runs while more experienced skiers can tackle the red and black pistes. The views from the top cable car station at 2,978m are absolutely world-class.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train in the late afternoon. Rest tired legs at the B&B, then enjoy a quiet evening in the village.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — eat a substantial breakfast before a full day of skiing.
meals.lunch: Bring packed lunch (sandwiches, energy bars, fruit) in a backpack to avoid expensive mountain restaurant prices. Eat at the base area picnic tables or in the ski lodge common area.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from Coop/Migros — pasta with local cheese sauce or risotto. Budget CHF 8–12 for ingredients. Many B&Bs allow use of a shared kitchen.

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza day ski pass costs approximately CHF 55–65 for adults. Book equipment rental online in advance for potential discounts. The train from Poschiavo to Diavolezza station takes about 40 minutes. This is the most expensive day of the trip — plan accordingly. Consider a half-day pass (afternoon) if budget is very tight, as it costs around CHF 40–45.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Morteratsch Glacier on foot — take the train to Morteratsch station (between Poschiavo and Pontresina) and follow the well-marked 1.5-hour glacier trail. The trail is free and leads you right up to the glacier snout, with marker posts showing how far the glacier has retreated over the decades. A humbling and spectacular experience in a dramatic mountain setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Pontresina, a charming alpine village and winter sports hub. Explore the village on foot, visit the Santa Maria Church with its medieval frescoes, and browse the local shops. Pontresina also has free cross-country skiing (langlauf) trails — if you have or can rent basic cross-country skis (CHF 20–25), this is a very budget-friendly way to enjoy winter sports.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the B&B, perhaps chatting with other guests about their alpine adventures.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Grab a bratwurst or hot snack from a local food stand in Pontresina (CHF 5–8), or bring packed lunch from the B&B.
meals.dinner: Try the local Graubünden specialty Capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings) at a village restaurant in Poschiavo. Budget CHF 18–22 for a main and a local beer or wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Morteratsch Glacier trail is approximately 3km each way and relatively flat — suitable for all fitness levels in winter boots. Wear waterproof footwear as the trail can be icy. The train from Poschiavo to Morteratsch station takes about 50 minutes. Pontresina is one stop further. Keep your Swiss Travel Pass or point-to-point tickets handy.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to St. Moritz — the world-famous luxury ski resort, just 30–40 minutes from Poschiavo by Bernina railway. While staying in budget accommodation in Poschiavo, you can enjoy St. Moritz as a day visitor. Start with a free walk around the frozen St. Moritzersee (Lake St. Moritz), which hosts events like horse racing and polo on ice in February. Explore the village and enjoy the glamorous atmosphere without spending a fortune.
day_by_day.afternoon: For a budget ski experience in St. Moritz, consider the Corviglia ski area — purchase a half-day afternoon pass (approximately CHF 50–60). Alternatively, enjoy free winter activities like sledding on public slopes, ice skating on the lake (if open, CHF 5–10 entry), or simply hiking the snowy trails above the village with panoramic Engadin valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Before returning to Poschiavo, treat yourself to a hot chocolate or coffee at one of St. Moritz's more affordable cafés (avoid the luxury hotel bars). Return to Poschiavo by early evening train.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: St. Moritz has a Coop supermarket — grab a budget lunch there (CHF 8–12) rather than eating at the expensive resort restaurants.
meals.dinner: Celebrate your penultimate evening with a slightly more indulgent dinner at the B&B's recommended local restaurant or a Poschiavo trattoria. Try local Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and a main for CHF 22–28.

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of the world's most expensive ski resorts, but visiting as a day tripper from budget Poschiavo is a smart way to experience it without the luxury price tag. The contrast between staying in affordable Poschiavo and visiting St. Moritz is one of the best budget travel hacks in the region. Saturday may be busier on the slopes — arrive early for shorter lift queues.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the B&B. Take a short farewell walk through Poschiavo village and up to the viewpoint above the town for one last panoramic view of the Valposchiavo valley, surrounding peaks, and the village below. Pack your bags and check out of the B&B.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, take the scenic Bernina Express train back toward Chur or toward Tirano (Italy) for connections. If time allows before your train, visit the Poschiavo Museum (Museo di Poschiavo) for a budget-friendly (CHF 5–8) look at the local history, culture, and the story of the Bernina railway. A fitting farewell to this unique Swiss-Italian alpine corner.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to your departure airport (Zurich or Milan Malpensa). Reflect on an incredible week of alpine adventure — skiing at Diavolezza, glacier walks, the Bernina Pass, St. Moritz, and the charming village of Poschiavo — all on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Final included breakfast at B&B — enjoy it fully before checkout.
meals.lunch: Pack leftover snacks or grab a final Coop/Migros meal at the train station for CHF 8–12.
meals.dinner: Airport or train station meal — budget CHF 15–20 for a simple meal before your flight home.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at most Swiss B&Bs is 10:00–11:00. Store luggage at Poschiavo train station if needed (luggage lockers available). The Bernina Express is a bucket-list train journey — even on the return trip, sit on the right side of the train heading toward Chur for the best views of the Landwasser Viaduct. Book return train tickets in advance on SBB.ch. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights): CHF 600–800 per person, including accommodation, transport, ski passes, meals, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Check in, settle into your room, and get a good night's rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama around 23:30–00:00 depending on transfer. Grab a light snack if available at the B&B or from any provisions you carry. Rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.dinner: Light snack upon arrival — pick up something at the airport (Migros or Coop convenience store) before the transfer to Poschiavo

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo is located in the Graubünden canton, roughly 1.5–2 hours from Zurich Airport via train (Bernina Express connection) or ~2 hours by car. Pre-arrange a taxi or rental car for the late-night arrival as public transport may be limited after 22:30. Confirm B&B late check-in arrangements in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely B&B breakfast and take a relaxed orientation walk through the charming village of Poschiavo. Explore the historic Piazza Comunale, the Spanish Quarter with its colorful Italianate architecture, and the frozen Lago di Poschiavo lakeside trail. This gentle start helps you acclimatize to the alpine altitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Livigno ski area (approx. 45 minutes by car via the Forcola di Livigno pass) or explore the local Diavolezza ski area (approx. 30 minutes from Poschiavo). Diavolezza offers excellent intermediate slopes with jaw-dropping views of the Bernina massif and Morteratsch Glacier — perfect for your first ski day. Rent equipment on-site if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo and dine at a local restaurant in the village. Explore the cozy streets of the old town before heading back to the B&B.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast at the Berninapass Panorama — expect fresh bread, cold cuts, cheese, yogurt, and hot drinks
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Diavolezza ski area — try a hearty Rösti with cheese or a warming bowl of Minestrone soup (CHF 18–28)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse or Al Cervo in Poschiavo — traditional Graubünden cuisine featuring pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta), polenta, and local meats (CHF 25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza ski pass costs approximately CHF 60–70 per day. Ski rental on-site is around CHF 40–55. Check snow conditions and lift status before heading out. The Bernina Pass road may require snow chains — confirm with the B&B host.

day_by_day.morning: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience — Drive approximately 30 minutes north to St. Moritz. Begin your morning with ice skating on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz, one of the most iconic winter experiences in Switzerland. Skate rental is available on-site. The lake setting surrounded by snowy peaks is absolutely magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, experience the historic Olympia Bob Run — one of the world's oldest and most famous bobsled tracks, dating back to 1904. You can ride as a passenger with a professional pilot for an unforgettable adrenaline rush reaching speeds of up to 130 km/h. Alternatively, explore the Corviglia ski area above St. Moritz for afternoon skiing with panoramic Engadin valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore St. Moritz village — window-shop the luxury boutiques on Via Serlas, then head to a mid-range restaurant for dinner before the scenic 30-minute drive back to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast at Berninahaus Panorama before departing for St. Moritz
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Bar Hauser in St. Moritz — a beloved local institution serving sandwiches, soups, and Swiss pastries at reasonable prices (CHF 15–25)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Engiadina in St. Moritz or a local trattoria — try Capuns (Swiss chard rolls with spätzle) or a classic Engadin nut tart for dessert (CHF 30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bobsled ride costs approximately CHF 120–150 per person — book in advance online as slots fill quickly. Ice skating entry and rental is around CHF 10–20. St. Moritz is a luxury resort town but has mid-range dining options if you look beyond the main hotel restaurants. Parking is available near the lake.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure — Drive approximately 2.5 hours west toward Les Diablerets (or take the scenic Bernina Express train to Chur and connect). Ride the iconic cable car to Glacier 3000 at 3,000 meters above sea level. Enjoy panoramic views spanning four countries — Switzerland, France, Italy, and Germany. The Peak Walk suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks is a must-do.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the glacier plateau — try the Snow Bus (a monster truck on snow), go sledding on the glacier, or ski the high-altitude glacier slopes. The glacier offers year-round skiing and is particularly spectacular in February. Take time to walk the Peak Walk by Tissot bridge for breathtaking 360-degree alpine views.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey to Poschiavo. Given the distance, consider stopping for dinner in Chur or Davos on the way back, or pick up provisions for a simple dinner at the B&B.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast before the longer drive — pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Restaurant on the Glacier 3000 plateau — Botta 3000 restaurant offers stunning views with Swiss mountain cuisine; try the glacier fondue or a warming soup (CHF 25–35)
meals.dinner: Stop at a restaurant in Chur on the return journey — try Zum Alten Zollhaus for traditional Graubünden cuisine (CHF 25–40), or pick up a Coop/Migros ready meal for a relaxed evening at the B&B

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 cable car return ticket costs approximately CHF 49–59 per adult. The Snow Bus experience is an additional CHF 10–15. This is a long day with significant driving — consider whether to do this as a day trip or break it into two days. Alternatively, the Glacier 3000 experience can be swapped for a closer activity if the drive feels too ambitious. Check road conditions on the A13 and mountain passes.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking — Take the scenic Bernina Express train from Poschiavo toward Chur, then connect to Interlaken for the Jungfrau region (approximately 3–3.5 hours total by train — a spectacular journey in itself). Join a guided snowshoe tour through the pristine alpine landscapes around Grindelwald or Wengen, with iconic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided snowshoe experience through the afternoon, exploring hidden winter trails and frozen waterfalls. The guide will share knowledge about alpine ecology, local traditions, and mountain safety. Alternatively, take the Jungfraujoch cogwheel railway to the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m for extraordinary glacier views.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo — the evening Bernina Express journey through the snow-covered Engadin valley is magical with winter lighting. Arrive back at the B&B for a well-deserved rest.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast before catching the morning train from Poschiavo
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or mountain hut lunch during the snowshoe tour — many guided tours include a stop at a traditional alpine hut (Berghütte) for hot drinks and simple food (CHF 15–20 if not included)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the B&B if the host offers evening meals, or at a local Poschiavo restaurant — try Osteria Salis for regional Valposchiavo specialties (CHF 25–35)

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfrau snowshoe experience costs approximately CHF 45–75 per person including guide. Book in advance through the Jungfrau region tourism website. The Bernina Express is a UNESCO World Heritage railway — book seats in advance (CHF 30–50 for the scenic panoramic car). This is a train-heavy day but the journey itself is a highlight. Alternatively, rent a car for more flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass — Take an early train or drive toward Zermatt (approximately 3 hours from Poschiavo via Chur and Visp). Zermatt is car-free, so park at Täsch and take the shuttle train. Begin skiing the world-famous slopes with over 360km of marked runs and the iconic Matterhorn as your backdrop. The views from the Klein Matterhorn at 3,883m are absolutely unforgettable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing Zermatt's varied terrain — from gentle blue runs on the Sunnegga plateau to challenging red and black runs on the Rothorn and Schwarzsee areas. Take a gondola up to the Glacier Paradise for the highest skiing in the Alps. Don't miss a photo stop with the Matterhorn in the background.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the vibrant après-ski atmosphere in Zermatt village — the Bahnhofstrasse is lined with cozy bars and restaurants. Have dinner before taking the shuttle train back to Täsch and driving back to Poschiavo (or consider staying overnight in Zermatt to avoid the long return drive).

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast or grab a croissant and coffee at the Poschiavo train station café
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch on the slopes — try Chez Vrony on the Findeln piste, famous for its stunning Matterhorn views and excellent Swiss cuisine; expect CHF 30–45 for a main course
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zermatt village — Walliserkanne restaurant offers excellent mid-range Swiss and Valaisan cuisine including raclette and local wines (CHF 35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt ski day pass costs approximately CHF 85–95 per adult. This is the most expensive ski day of the trip but absolutely worth it. Book lift passes online in advance for a small discount. The drive back to Poschiavo from Täsch is approximately 2.5–3 hours — consider whether to return that evening or book a budget hotel in Zermatt/Visp for the night. Saturday is the busiest day on the slopes — arrive early to beat the crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening (afternoon/evening experience) — Start your final morning with a relaxed farewell walk around Poschiavo. Visit the local Sunday market if running, explore the Museo di Poschiavo to learn about the valley's unique Italian-Swiss cultural heritage, and take a final stroll along the Lago di Poschiavo lakeside path with your camera.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take the train toward Verbier (approximately 3 hours) for the Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening experience. Alternatively, if the distance is too far for a final day, arrange a similar fondue experience closer to Poschiavo — ask your B&B host to recommend a local chalet dinner. Enjoy a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner in a historic mountain chalet, learning about cheese-making traditions and Swiss alpine culture.
day_by_day.evening: Conclude your Swiss Alps adventure with this warm, convivial cultural dinner experience — the perfect farewell to Switzerland. Toast with local Fendant white wine or Rivella. Begin your return journey or rest at the B&B for an early departure the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Final full B&B breakfast at Berninapass Panorama — savor the mountain views one last time
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Poschiavo village — Café del Borgo or a local bakery for fresh bread, local cheese, and cold cuts (CHF 10–18)
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening in a historic mountain chalet — traditional fondue moitié-moitié (Gruyère and Vacherin), raclette, and local charcuterie with regional wines (CHF 55–75 per person including the cultural experience)

day_by_day.notes: The fondue cultural evening should be booked in advance. If Verbier is too far for Day 7, contact the experience provider to see if they offer the experience in closer locations such as Davos or St. Moritz. Alternatively, your B&B host may be able to arrange a private fondue evening locally. Pack your bags the night before if you have an early departure. The Bernina Express back toward Zurich runs regularly and is a beautiful final journey through the Alps.

day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Enjoy a light welcome amenity or room service if available. Rest and prepare for the week ahead in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit or airport dining (e.g., SWISS Business Lounge at Zurich Airport)
meals.dinner: Light in-room dining or welcome snack board arranged by the B&B upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (e.g., via Swiss Limousine Service or Blacklane) from Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport to Poschiavo — approximately 2–3 hours depending on origin airport. Confirm late check-in with the property in advance. Pack ski gear or arrange rental bookings for the following days.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the B&B to recover from travel. Take a scenic morning stroll through the charming village of Poschiavo, a UNESCO-listed heritage town with Italianate architecture and frozen alpine vistas. Explore the historic Piazza Comunale and the Church of San Vittore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or arrange a private transfer to the nearby Livigno ski area (approx. 45 minutes from Poschiavo via the Bernina Pass road). Enjoy an introductory afternoon ski session on Livigno's well-groomed slopes — a tax-free alpine resort with excellent intermediate and advanced runs. Rent premium ski equipment on-site if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a refined dinner at a local upscale restaurant. Explore Ristorante Suisse or a curated dining experience in the village center featuring regional Graubünden cuisine — think venison ragù, barley soup (Bündner Gerstensuppe), and local Poschiavo wines.

meals.breakfast: Full alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass — fresh bread, local cheeses, cold cuts, jams, and hot beverages
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Livigno ski area — try Ristorante Camana Veglia for rustic alpine cuisine with panoramic views
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium local restaurant in Poschiavo — regional Graubünden specialties paired with Valtellina or Swiss Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Check Bernina Pass road conditions before driving — the pass may require snow chains in February. Livigno is technically in Italy but easily accessible and offers duty-free shopping. Book ski rentals in advance for premium equipment (e.g., Völkl or Rossignol race-grade skis).

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private transfer to St. Moritz (approx. 45 minutes from Poschiavo via the Maloja Pass or Bernina Express route). Begin the morning with the St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience — glide across the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz, one of the most iconic winter settings in the world, surrounded by the Engadin mountain panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: After skating, take on the historic Olympia Bob Run — one of the oldest and only natural ice bobsled tracks in the world. Experience the adrenaline of reaching speeds up to 130 km/h on a guided public bob taxi ride. Afterward, explore the glamorous St. Moritz village — browse luxury boutiques on Via Serlas (Cartier, Bulgari, Hermès) and soak in the elite alpine atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a world-class dinner in St. Moritz before returning to Poschiavo. Dine at Ecco St. Moritz (2 Michelin stars) at Giardino Mountain for an extraordinary contemporary Alpine cuisine experience, or opt for the iconic Kulm Hotel's Restaurant Sunny Bar for classic Swiss elegance.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B before departure — or grab a coffee and pastry at a St. Moritz café upon arrival (e.g., Café Hanselmann, est. 1894)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mathis Food Affairs at Chesa Veglia in St. Moritz — a historic 17th-century farmhouse serving refined Swiss and Italian cuisine
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Ecco St. Moritz (Giardino Mountain Hotel) — 2 Michelin stars, tasting menu with wine pairing; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Book the Olympia Bob Run taxi rides in advance at olympia-bobrun.ch — slots fill quickly in peak season. The bob run typically operates mornings and afternoons. Dress in warm, windproof layers for both skating and bobsledding. Private transfer recommended for the return journey to Poschiavo in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Zermatt — depart early by private transfer or scenic train journey (via Chur and the Glacier Express corridor, approximately 3–4 hours, or private car ~2.5 hours). Arrive in the car-free village of Zermatt and begin the Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass experience. Take the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car to 3,883m for breathtaking views of the iconic Matterhorn peak and ski the world-famous slopes across 360km of marked runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on Zermatt's varied terrain — from the high-altitude glacier runs to the tree-lined lower slopes. Explore the Klein Matterhorn area and the Italian border runs connecting to Cervinia. Take a mid-afternoon break at a mountain restaurant to rest and refuel with panoramic Matterhorn views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Zermatt before the return journey — dine at Restaurant Chez Vrony on the Findeln slope (accessible by ski or gondola), renowned for its raclette, local Valais wines, and unobstructed Matterhorn views. Alternatively, dine at the Michelin-starred After Seven restaurant for contemporary Alpine fine dining. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at B&B before departure
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at Zermatt's Schwarzsee Restaurant or Gandegghütte at 3,029m — fondue, rösti, and hot chocolate with glacier views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Chez Vrony, Findeln, Zermatt — iconic raclette and Valais specialties with Matterhorn backdrop

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — park at Täsch and take the shuttle train (8 minutes) into the village, or arrange a full private transfer door-to-door. Purchase the Zermatt ski pass online in advance. Altitude at the glacier (3,883m) can cause mild altitude sickness — stay hydrated and ascend gradually. Ski helmet and high-SPF sunscreen are essential at glacier altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Depart for the Jungfrau Region (approximately 2.5–3 hours by private transfer from Poschiavo via Interlaken). Begin the Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking experience — join a certified mountain guide for a guided snowshoe trek through the pristine alpine landscapes around Grindelwald or Mürren. Traverse snow-laden forests, frozen meadows, and dramatic cliff-edge trails with views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the snowshoe tour, take the Jungfraujoch cogwheel train to the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m — Europe's highest railway station. Explore the Ice Palace, the Sphinx Observatory viewing platform, and the eternal snow fields of the Aletsch Glacier, the longest glacier in the Alps. A truly unmissable alpine spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Descend to Grindelwald or Interlaken for a premium dinner before returning to Poschiavo. Dine at the Michelin-recommended Restaurant Schmitte in Grindelwald or the elegant Victoria-Jungfrau Grand Hotel & Spa's La Terrasse restaurant in Interlaken for refined Swiss cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B before early departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Restaurant — a unique dining experience at 3,454m altitude; or pack a premium picnic prepared by the B&B
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Terrasse, Victoria-Jungfrau Grand Hotel, Interlaken — classic French-Swiss cuisine in a Belle Époque setting

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance at jungfrau.ch — the 'Good Morning Ticket' offers early access at a reduced rate. Dress in extreme cold-weather layers for the Jungfraujoch (temperatures can reach -20°C with wind chill). The snowshoe tour guide should be pre-booked through Jungfrau Region tourism or a certified alpine guide service.

day_by_day.morning: Depart for Les Diablerets / Glacier 3000 (approximately 3 hours from Poschiavo by private transfer). Embark on the Glacier 3000 Cable Car & Snow Bus Adventure — ride the iconic Peak Walk cable car to 3,000m above sea level for sweeping panoramic views across four countries (Switzerland, France, Italy, and Germany). Walk the thrilling Peak Walk suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks — the only such bridge in the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience the Snow Bus — a unique monster-truck-style vehicle that traverses the glacier plateau. Optionally ski or snowboard on the glacier's varied terrain, or try the glacier's snow tubing and sledding runs for a fun afternoon. Visit the Col du Pillon area and explore the charming village of Gstaad nearby — one of Switzerland's most exclusive alpine resorts — for luxury boutique browsing and a warm drink at a chic café.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a lavish dinner in Gstaad before returning to Poschiavo. Dine at the legendary Chesery Restaurant in Gstaad (1 Michelin star) — a beloved institution serving refined French-Swiss cuisine in a cozy chalet atmosphere, frequented by royalty and celebrities. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Glacier 3000 summit restaurant — panoramic glacier views with Swiss mountain cuisine (rösti, soups, and hot drinks)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Chesery, Gstaad — Michelin-starred French-Swiss cuisine with an exceptional wine cellar; reserve in advance

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 tickets can be purchased at glacier3000.ch — combo packages including cable car and Snow Bus are available. The Peak Walk bridge is weather-dependent and may close in high winds. Gstaad is approximately 20 minutes from Les Diablerets — a worthwhile detour for the ultra-luxury alpine village experience. Dress warmly; glacier winds can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — enjoy a leisurely, indulgent breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Take a relaxed morning walk through Poschiavo village one last time, visiting the local weekly market if available, and pick up artisan souvenirs — local cheeses, Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart), and regional wines. Attend the Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening experience (if rescheduled to a farewell lunch format) or arrange a private fondue lunch at a local chalet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in the Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Evening experience as a farewell afternoon activity — join a traditional Swiss fondue and raclette dinner in a historic mountain chalet, learning about Swiss cheese-making traditions and alpine culinary culture. A warm, convivial send-off to an extraordinary week in the Alps.
day_by_day.evening: Pack, check out, and depart for the airport via private luxury transfer. Reflect on an unforgettable week of world-class skiing, glacier adventures, Michelin-starred dining, and iconic Swiss alpine experiences. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at B&B — full spread with local Graubünden specialties, fresh pastries, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Swiss Alpine Cheese & Fondue Cultural Experience — traditional fondue moitié-moitié, raclette, and Swiss wines in a historic mountain chalet
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — or an early dinner at a restaurant near the departure airport if time permits

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with B&B and arrange luggage storage if the fondue experience runs into the afternoon. Allow ample transfer time to the airport (Zurich: ~2.5–3 hours; Milan Malpensa: ~2 hours from Poschiavo). Purchase any last-minute Swiss souvenirs in Poschiavo village — the local shops carry excellent regional products. Consider booking the fondue experience in Verbier or a nearby chalet as listed in the available experiences.
